name: Portugal — Portuguese parties
intro: compare it with Portuguese political parties in 2025
inclusion_note: The test includes the parties that received more than 7,000 votes in the 2024 legislative elections (the minimum number of signatures needed to form a political party in Portugal).
hemicycle_note: Seats in the Assembly of the Republic after the May 2025 legislative election, arranged left to right. 230 MPs.

PS.name: Socialist Party
PS.priorities: Strengthening the welfare state (NHS, education), Income redistribution, Pro-Europeanism
PS.description: Portugal's main centre-left party, a defender of the welfare state and a member of the Party of European Socialists. It seeks to balance social policies with sustainable economic growth.

AD.name: Democratic Alliance — PPD-PSD/CDS-PP coalition
AD.ideologies: Liberal conservatism, Christian democracy, Economic liberalism
AD.priorities: Tax cuts (personal and corporate income tax), Maintaining the welfare state, Economic growth, Public debt control
AD.description: Centre-right coalition led by the Social Democratic Party (PPD/PSD), also including CDS-PP. It advocates a market economy with social responsibility, reforms to boost competitiveness, and government stability.

Chega.name: Chega ("Enough")
Chega.priorities: Reducing immigration, Fighting corruption and "the system", Strengthening security and State authority, Tax cuts
Chega.description: Radical-right party whose discourse centres on defending national identity, security, criticism of the political system and anti-immigration positions. It defends conservative and nationalist values and economic liberalism.

IL.name: Liberal Initiative
IL.priorities: Cutting taxes and red tape, Economic and individual freedom, State reform, Privatisations
IL.description: Liberal party advocating limited State intervention in the economy and society. It proposes market liberalisation and deregulation, privatising most state-owned companies, significantly lower taxes and greater individual freedom of choice.

CDU.name: Unitary Democratic Coalition (Portuguese Communist Party + Ecologist Party "The Greens")
CDU.priorities: Workers' rights, Universal and free public services, Nationalisations, National sovereignty, Opposition to NATO and the European Union
CDU.description: Permanent alliance between the Portuguese Communist Party (PCP) and the Ecologist Party "The Greens" (PEV). It defends workers' interests, a stronger public sector and national sovereignty. The PCP maintains a Marxist-Leninist line.

Livre.name: Livre ("Free")
Livre.ideologies: Socialism, Progressivism, Ecology, Pro-Europeanism, Minority rights
Livre.priorities: Income redistribution, Fighting climate change, Minority rights, Housing, Universal Basic Income (UBI)
Livre.description: Left-wing party with a strong emphasis on ecology, human rights, deepening democracy and greater European integration. It advocates inclusive social policies and a socialist economic model focused on sustainability. Known for its leadership model with rotating spokespersons.

PAN.name: People-Animals-Nature
PAN.priorities: Animal and environmental protection, One Health (human/animal/environmental), Fighting climate change, Human rights
PAN.description: Party focused on animal rights and environmental protection as its central pillars. It promotes sustainability policies, animal welfare, ecosystem preservation and a green economy. It generally aligns with the centre-left on social issues.

BE.name: Left Bloc
BE.priorities: Strengthening public services (NHS, schools), Labour rights, Income redistribution, Nationalisations
BE.description: Radical-left party, critical of liberalism and advocating socialist and ecological alternatives. It resulted from the merger of several left-wing movements. Strong emphasis on minority rights and social justice.

ADN.name: National Democratic Alternative
ADN.priorities: Fighting corruption, Reducing the State, National sovereignty, Anti-vaccine positions, Opposition to "global agendas"
ADN.description: Formerly the Democratic Republican Party. Conservative and nationalist party, highly critical of the current political system, of the State's role in society, of international organisations and agendas (World Health Organization, climate, etc.) and of scientific consensus.

RIR.name: React-Include-Recycle
RIR.priorities: Reform of the political/justice system, Transparency, Fighting corruption
RIR.description: Presents itself as an alternative to the centre-left and centre-right parties, focusing on reforming the justice and political systems to increase transparency and democratic representation. Generally holds moderate positions in other areas.

JPP.name: Together for the People
JPP.description: Party with a strong base in Madeira, focused on defending the region's interests and fighting for greater autonomy. Holds pragmatic, centrist positions locally.

Nova Direita.name: New Right
Nova Direita.ideologies: Christian conservatism, Anti-immigration, Economic liberalism, Nationalism
Nova Direita.priorities: Reducing immigration, Tax cuts, Security, Defence of the traditional family, Public debt control
Nova Direita.description: Party founded by CDS-PP dissidents. Presents itself as socially conservative and economically liberal, defending right-wing values.

PCTP/MRPP.name: Portuguese Workers' Communist Party
PCTP/MRPP.priorities: Socialist revolution, Dictatorship of the proletariat, Anti-imperialism
PCTP/MRPP.description: Maoist party that maintains a classic revolutionary discourse advocating the nationalisation of the means of production.

Volt.name: Volt Portugal
Volt.ideologies: Social liberalism, Progressivism, European federalism, Ecology
Volt.priorities: EU reform, Digital and climate transition, Pragmatic social policies, Human rights
Volt.description: Portuguese branch of the pan-European Volt Europa movement. It advocates a free-market economy complemented by a strong welfare state, based on progressive, evidence-based policies and best practices. It supports a more integrated and democratic European Union.
